escalation.rationale: US-Iran war enters 13th consecutive night of intensified fighting with Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabia, a second US-disabled merchant vessel enforcing the Hormuz blockade, Iranian missile strikes on US bases in Jordan, and expanded US air campaign scope, sustaining near-critical escalation pressure across the Middle East.

ticker_items: US disables second merchant vessel breaching Iran port blockade in Hormuz Strait.
Houthis claim missile strike on Jizan, southern Saudi Arabia, escalating regional war.
Iran reportedly launches missiles and drones at Aqaba, Jordan, targeting US military sites.
Netanyahu to meet Trump at White House next week amid ongoing Iran war.
US withholds $400M in Ukraine military aid approved by Congress until FY2029.

new_entrant.text: Jordan has emerged as a direct target of Iranian missile and drone strikes, with attacks on Aqaba and its airport prompting air defense intercepts, marking a significant geographic expansion of the US-Iran conflict.

eastern_europe.description: Ukrainian drone or missile strike reportedly created a crater outside Moscow, per crowdsourced reporting.

middle_east.description: Iran launched missiles and drones targeting the Red Sea port city of Aqaba and its airport, prompting Jordanian air defense responses.
Houthi rebels claimed a missile strike on the southern Saudi city of Jizan hours after Saudi-led forces struck Houthi military sites in Yemen.
US military disabled a second merchant vessel attempting to breach the US blockade of Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz.
US expanded its air campaign beyond naval and coastal targets to broader Iranian military infrastructure following collapse of a ceasefire over the Strait of Hormuz.
Israel carried out blasts across south Lebanon despite an ongoing ceasefire framework under negotiation with Lebanese officials.
Saudi-led forces struck Houthi military positions in Yemen, prompting retaliatory missile claims against Saudi territory.

observers.description: Taoiseach Micheál Martin visited Kyiv expressing support for Ukraine's EU membership ambitions. Ireland faces diplomatic pressure over Aughinish Alumina, a Rusal-owned plant potentially supplying aluminium usable in Russian weapons, with an unpublished EU sanctions risk report now in focus.

North Korea reaffirmed support for Russia at a Moscow foreign ministers' meeting, with speculation growing about a possible Kim Jong Un visit to the Kremlin. North Korea's military partnership with Russia, part of the 'axis of upheaval', is assessed by analysts as durable beyond the Ukraine conflict.

Reports indicate China is pushing diplomatically for an end to the US-Iran war, contributing to a drop in crude oil prices on Friday. China remains part of Russia's broader 'axis of upheaval' partnership while seeking to mediate the Gulf crisis.

RAF Fairford hosted US B-1 bombers used in strikes against Iran this week, prompting emergency protests by CND and Fairford Action groups. Iran's foreign ministry issued a statement referencing the UK base's role, raising concerns about British exposure to Iranian retaliation.

Saudi Arabia's forces struck Houthi military sites in Yemen and received a retaliatory Houthi missile strike on Jizan. Saudi Arabia is increasingly entangled in the broader US-Iran war despite diplomatic complexities with Washington.

The US expanded its air campaign against Iran for a 13th consecutive night of fighting, enforcing a naval blockade on Iranian ports and disabling a second merchant vessel. Domestically, the White House is withholding $400M in Ukraine military aid until FY2029, signalling reallocation of strategic focus to Iran.

financial.notes: Crude oil futures fell Friday on reports that China is pushing for an end to the US-Iran war, though Brent posted significant weekly gains driven by Hormuz Strait shipping disruptions and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
